does: Cuts a thin sheet of rolled pasta dough into ribbons, strips or squares of even size, so that they cook at the same speed.

intro.what: A rolled pasta sheet is cut into even ribbons or other shapes, then separated before it sticks.
intro.why: The surface needs to be dry enough to release, yet flexible enough to fold. Consistent cuts help the pieces cook at a similar pace.

how: Roll the dough out thin and let the sheet dry for a short while, until it feels leathery and no longer sticks.
Dust the sheet lightly with flour, then fold it loosely into a flat roll, or leave it as a sheet.
With a long, sharp knife cut straight across at the width the dish needs: narrow for ribbons, broad for short strips.
Shake the cut pieces loose, toss them in a little flour and lay them in loose heaps or nests on a floured tray.

cues.text: The strips are of even width, with clean edges, and they fall apart when shaken.
The sheet folds without sticking to itself.

mistakes.mistake: Cutting a sheet that is still sticky, so that the pieces glue together.
mistakes.fix: Let it dry a little and dust it with flour.

mistakes.mistake: Cutting strips of uneven width, so that the thin ones are soft before the wide ones are ready.
mistakes.fix: Cut with a long knife and a steady hand, in straight lines.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving cut pasta in a damp heap, so that it sticks into a lump.
mistakes.fix: Toss it in flour and lay it loosely in nests.

quiz.question: Why keep the cut pasta strips an even width?
choices: They cook at a similar pace.
Narrow strips should soften before broad strips.
Uneven edges prevent the pasta from sticking.
quiz.because: Consistent width limits differences in how quickly the strips soften.

quiz.question: What condition should the sheet reach before loose folding and cutting?
choices: Wet enough to glue itself together.
Brittle enough to snap when folded.
quiz.because: A flexible dry surface folds without sticking or breaking.

quiz.question: What should happen when the cut strips are shaken?
choices: They remain glued into a flat roll.
quiz.because: Clean separate strips show that the surface and cuts allow the pasta to release.

quiz.question: The cut pasta stuck into a damp lump on the tray. What would you change next time?
choices: Dust it lightly and arrange it in loose nests.
Press the damp strips into a tighter heap.
Wet the tray before laying the strips down.
quiz.because: Light flour and loose placement keep damp surfaces from resting tightly together.

comes_after.why: Pasta is cut from a sheet that has first been rolled evenly thin.
